baseline:
B
A standard Transformer block consists of a multi-head attention mechanism and a position-wise feedforward network (which is a type of MLP).

B
An MLP is defined by its structure, which includes an input layer, an output layer, and at least one hidden layer. The use of non-linear activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) in these hidden layers is crucial, as it enables the network to learn and model complex, non-linear relationships in the data.

B
The MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron), also known as the Position-wise Feed-Forward Network, processes the output of the attention layer. This output consists of context-aware embeddings, and the MLP applies a non-linear transformation to each embedding individually to further refine and enrich the information.

C
The MLP (feed-forward network) component acts as a key-value memory. Its weights are trained to recognize specific input patterns (keys) from the preceding attention layer and transform them into corresponding output patterns (values), effectively storing and recalling factual associations.

C
The training process of an MLP adjusts the weights (W) and biases (b) to capture patterns in the data. These learned parameter values are the mechanism by which the network stores and represents the "facts" or knowledge it has acquired.
